_exec_summary.SummaryText:
Executive Summary, Stillwater RMP

Ormat Stillwater, LLC ("Ormat") has provided a written Emergency Action Plan for its facility and required employee implementation based on the belief that it is a valuable resource for the safety and well-being of all Ormat personnel and property. Ormat believes that no monetary value can be placed above a human life and, therefore, will provide procedures for the primary purpose of preserving life and secondly to preserve its assets at this location. 
Ormat expects its employees to respond only to incidental releases of hazardous substances and not to major, uncontrollable releases where employees are expected to immediately evacuate the site. Therefore, an Emergency Action Plan, which is an element of the Emergency Response Plan, has been developed to detail the evacuation procedures. 
The Stillwater Geothermal Power Plant is a binary geothermal power generation facility built on a combination of Ormat owned property, private leases, and Bureau of Land Management leases within the Stillwater Known Geothermal Resource Area (KGRA). The project is designed to produce approximately 47.2 MW gross output (Unit Nameplate Gross Capacity 11.8 MW x 4). 
A binary geothermal plant operates utilizing two closed loop systems that exchange heat energy. The first loop is geothermal fluid that is pumped from production wells to the plant. This hot geothermal brine passes through a series of heat exchangers where a portion of its heat energy is given up and then flows to injection wells where it is pumped back into the underground resource. The second loop is the motive fluid, in this case isobutane, which is pumped from an accumulator vessel, as a liquid, to the heat exchangers where heat from the geothermal fluid vaporizes the isobutane to a superheated vapor. In the vapor state, it passes through a turbine which drives a generator that produces electrical energy. Having passed through the turbine, the vapor, at reduced temperature and pressure

, flows through air cooled condensers where additional heat is removed, resulting in the isobutane returning to a liquid state. The liquid isobutane gravity drains back to the accumulator vessel from which the cycle begins again.  During normal operation, the isobutane and geothermal fluid are never in direct contact and are not lost to the atmosphere.	
Ormat complies with all requirements of Nevada's Department of Environmental Protection Chemical Accident Prevention Program ("CAPP"). Additionally, the CAPP program contains all elements of OSHA's PSM Standard 29 CFR, Part 1910.199(c) and EPA RMP Standard 40 CFR, Part 68.83. Program elements of CAPP are administered by Ormat's Environmental Compliance Coordinator and implemented on a day to day basis by the site Plant Manager. Employees are aware of, have access to, and are included in the development and implementation of all of the following program elements: Process Safety Information, Process Hazard Analysis, Standard Operating Procedures/Safe Work Practices, Management of Change, Pre Startup Safety Review, Incident Investigation, Emergency Action/Response Plan, Contractor Safety Training, Preventative Maintenance/Mechanical Integrity, Employee Participation, and Compliance Audit programs. 
Ormat also has incorporated safety systems into the design of the Stillwater Geothermal Plant that enhance the overall safety of the operation. Specific measures include an emergency shutdown system which brings all plant processes to a halt in a timely and safe manner, combustible gas and fire detectors, fire water system, and both audible and visual alarms, designed to alert personnel to emergency conditions and prevent accidental releases of isobutane. An evacuation system reduces emissions by allowing for storage of isobutane during maintenance activities. 
Stillwater has had no accidental releases of isobutane since startup in June 2010 and, with careful implementation of its safety program elements and its robust design

features, has a minimal probability of future accidental releases. If an accident were to occur, Ormat maintains emergency responder coordination with Fallon/Churchill Fire Department, Reno of Tri-County Hazmat, Churchill County Sheriff's Department and Banner-Churchill Community Hospital. Emergency response training is part of Ormat's overall Emergency Action Plan.
